title: 7 Church Potluck Pies That Vanished After 1970 (I Still Bake Them)
description:
Well, hello from my kitchen. These are the seven pies that were on every church supper table I ever knew, and I've written every one of them down for you right here, the way I make them. No boxes, no mixes. Just a nine inch pie plate and a little patience.

— Loretta

🥧 THE 7 PIES (each one is a 9-inch pie that cuts into 8 pieces)

1) CHESS PIE — unbaked crust · 350°F · 45–50 min
1 stick butter (½ cup), melted and cooled a little · 1 ½ cups sugar · 1 Tbsp yellow cornmeal · 1 Tbsp flour · pinch of salt · 4 eggs · ¼ cup milk · 1 Tbsp white vinegar · 1 tsp vanilla.
Stir the sugar, cornmeal, flour and salt together, stir in the butter, then the eggs one at a time (stir, don't beat), then the milk, vinegar and vanilla. Bake until golden with just a little wobble in the middle. Cool at least 3 hours before cutting.
Lemon chess: use the juice and grated peel of 1 lemon instead of the milk. Chocolate chess: add 3 Tbsp cocoa to the sugar.

2) SUGAR CREAM PIE — unbaked crust · 400°F 10 min, then 350°F about 45 min
1 cup sugar · ¼ cup flour · pinch of salt · 2 cups heavy cream · 1 tsp vanilla · 2 Tbsp butter in small pieces · fresh nutmeg. No eggs.
Mix the sugar, flour and salt dry right in the crust, pour the cream (with the vanilla) over it and stir gently with a clean finger, no beater. Dot with butter, grate nutmeg on top. Bake until it bubbles all over the top. It looks like soup when it comes out: let it set 4 hours on the counter or overnight in the icebox.

3) SHOOFLY PIE (wet bottom) — unbaked crust · 400°F 10 min, then 350°F about 30 min
Crumbs: 1 cup flour · ⅔ cup brown sugar · 4 Tbsp cold butter, rubbed together with your fingers.
Bottom: 1 cup light (mild) molasses, not blackstrap · 1 egg, beaten · ¾ cup boiling water · 1 tsp baking soda.
Dissolve the soda in the hot water first (it fizzes), stir it into the molasses and egg, pour into the crust, scatter the crumbs on top and don't stir. For dry bottom, bake about 10 minutes longer. Best the next morning with black coffee.

4) BUTTERSCOTCH PIE — baked crust · stovetop filling
1 cup dark brown sugar, packed · 4 Tbsp butter · 2 ½ cups whole milk · 3 Tbsp cornstarch · ¼ tsp salt · 3 egg yolks · 1 tsp vanilla.
Brown the butter in an iron skillet, stir in the brown sugar and cook it darker than you think. Warm 2 cups of the milk and pour it in slowly (it hisses). Whisk the cornstarch and salt into the last ½ cup of cold milk, then the yolks; stir into the skillet and cook until thick and bubbling, about 5 minutes. Off the heat, add vanilla. Pour into the baked crust.
Meringue: the 3 whites, a pinch of cream of tartar, 6 Tbsp sugar a spoon at a time; spread on the hot filling, sealed to the crust, 350°F about 12 minutes.

5) LEMON MERINGUE PIE — baked crust · meringue 350°F 12–15 min
1 cup sugar · ⅓ cup cornstarch · ¼ tsp salt · 1 ½ cups water · 4 egg yolks · ½ cup fresh lemon juice (about 3 lemons) · 1 Tbsp grated lemon peel · 2 Tbsp butter.
Cook the sugar, cornstarch, salt and water until thick and clear, boil 1 minute. Warm the beaten yolks with a little of the hot mixture, stir them back in and boil 2 more minutes. OFF the heat, stir in the lemon juice, peel and butter.
Meringue: 4 egg whites · ¼ tsp cream of tartar · ½ cup sugar, beaten to stiff glossy peaks. Pour the filling into the crust while it's HOT, spread the meringue on right away and push it out until it touches the crust all the way around. Bake until the peaks are golden.

6) SOUR CREAM RAISIN PIE — baked crust · meringue 350°F about 12 min
1 cup raisins · 1 cup sour cream · 1 cup milk · ¾ cup sugar · 3 Tbsp cornstarch · 3 egg yolks · 1 tsp cinnamon · 1 tsp vanilla.
Simmer the raisins in water for 5 minutes and drain them. Whisk the sugar, cornstarch and cinnamon with the sour cream, milk and yolks, and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick and bubbling, about 8 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the raisins and vanilla, pour into the crust while hot. Meringue of 3 whites and 6 Tbsp sugar, sealed to the crust.

7) MAMA'S MOCK APPLE PIE — two crusts · 425°F · 30–35 min
Pastry for a two-crust 9-inch pie · 36 round butter crackers · 2 cups water · 2 cups sugar · 2 tsp cream of tartar · 2 Tbsp lemon juice · grated peel of 1 lemon · 2 Tbsp butter · ½ tsp cinnamon.
Simmer the water, sugar and cream of tartar for 15 minutes; off the heat add the lemon juice and peel, and let the syrup cool all the way. Break the crackers by hand into big pieces (never crush them) into the bottom crust, pour the COOL syrup over them, dot with butter, sprinkle the cinnamon, put on the top crust and cut a few slits. Bake until crisp and golden and let it cool before cutting.

MY CRUST (one crust): 1 ¼ cups flour · ½ tsp salt · ½ cup cold shortening, lard or butter · 3–4 Tbsp ice water. Cut the fat in to pea-size, add ice water a spoon at a time, rest it 30 minutes in the icebox. For the cooked pies, bake it empty with paper and dry beans at 425°F for 15 minutes, then 5–10 more without the beans.

✨ THE LITTLE TRICK I MENTIONED
For any custard pie in an unbaked crust (chess, sugar cream, shoofly): beat one egg white with a fork until it's just foamy, brush a thin coat over the bottom and sides of the raw crust, and let it dry 10 minutes before you pour in the filling. It seals the dough so the bottom bakes crisp instead of soggy. I learned it too late for about thirty church suppers.

Keep it safe: every pie here except the mock apple has eggs or milk in it. Once they cool they go in the icebox, good for 3 to 4 days, and at a potluck don't leave a custard pie out more than a couple of hours.
